title: Collectible Coin Protection Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Collectible Coin Protection Act - Amends the Hobby Protection Act to make it a violation of such Act for a person to provide substantial assistance or support to any manufacturer, importer, or seller if that person knows or should have known that such manufacturer, importer, or seller has engaged in any act or practice that violates requirements for plainly identifying imitation political items or imitation coins and other numismatic items. Provides that if such a violation also involves the unauthorized use of registered trademarks belonging to a collectibles certification service, the owner of such trademarks shall also have all rights provided under appropriate provisions of the Trademark Act of 1946.

summary.headline: This law makes it illegal to knowingly help sellers who break labeling rules for imitation coins and political items, and it gives certification services more trademark protection.
summary.what_it_does: It changes the Hobby Protection Act, which requires certain fake coins and political items to be clearly marked as imitations. Under the change, a person can violate the law by giving substantial help or support to a maker, importer, or seller who breaks these labeling rules, if that person knew or should have known about the violation. If the violation also involves using registered trademarks owned by a collectibles certification service without permission, the trademark owner gets the same rights under the Trademark Act of 1946.

who_it_affects.group: Makers, importers, and sellers of imitation coins and other collectible numismatic items
who_it_affects.how: They must clearly identify imitation coins and related items, and they can face liability if they break those rules.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses that provide support services to sellers of collectible coins and imitation political items
who_it_affects.how: They can violate the law if they knowingly or carelessly give substantial help to a seller who breaks the labeling rules.
If someone uses their registered trademarks without permission in a labeling violation, they can use the trademark protections in the Trademark Act of 1946.

who_it_affects.group: Collectors who buy coins and numismatic items
who_it_affects.how: The labeling rules are meant to help buyers tell imitation items from genuine ones.
